index.html.title: Tomato — A functional 32-bit computer built from scratch in a dorm
index.html.description: A 32-bit computer designed from the logic level up in a dorm: ISA, OS, games, verification, and a fabricated ALU. Run it in the browser or text the machine.
index.html.imageAlt: KiCad render of the Tomato ALU circuit board

jsonLd.name: Tomato
jsonLd.description: A 32-bit computer designed from the logic level up in a dorm: Dual-LUT CPU on FPGA and discrete 74xx, Tomato OS, and a fabricated ALU. ASIC is a long-term goal.

verification.html.description: I drove 130 billion Verilator test vectors through the 32-bit ALU against a reference model in a 2 hour 45 minute run. Formal verification separately checks the ALU at 1, 8, and 32 bits. Methods, commands, and limits are here.

architecture.html.description: I built Tomato around a configurable 32-bit arithmetic and logic engine. Follow an instruction from memory, through the controls and calculation, to the register that keeps the result.

software.html.description: I write programs in Tomato assembly, assemble them into machine code, and run them on the FPGA computer. The next work is making more of the ALU’s compound operations useful through instruction mappings, compiler support, and better tools.

os.html.description: Tomato OS boots on the FPGA computer, draws the menu, reads the controls, and runs games. I wrote it in Tomato’s own assembly language. These recordings show the hardware and software working together.

playground.html.description: Two programmable truth tables feed one adder: f(A,B,C) + g(A,B,C) + carry. Try familiar operations, then build compound ones. The ALU has 524,288 control configurations; some produce the same function.

isa.html.title: Tomato ISA — Tomato
isa.html.description: Tomato ISA: 91 instructions plus NOP occupy 92 burned rows in a 512-row instruction ROM. The authoritative tomato.v1.csv maps native mnemonics onto the Dual-LUT datapath.

journal.html.description: My record of designing, testing, soldering, and programming Tomato. These entries capture the project at the time they were written—including ideas that changed along the way.

gallery.html.description: See Tomato OS on screen, the ALU board being assembled, and the designs behind the hardware. These are recordings and photographs from my build.

board.html.description: Rotate the Lot 07 ALU model to inspect the chips, traces, and connectors. This board implements an 8-bit slice of Tomato’s 32-bit arithmetic and logic engine.

viewer.html.description: Immersive full-screen 3D tour of Tomato 07_alu PCB — top, iso, bottom copper, mask peel, keyboard shortcuts.

boards.html.description: I designed the architecture to be built from off-the-shelf logic and memory chips. The Lot 07 ALU board is soldered. The remaining boards are progressing alongside the software ecosystem on the working FPGA.

about.html.description: I’m a Computer Engineering student at the University of Pennsylvania, Class of 2028. I started with an 8-bit ALU and kept building toward a computer whose hardware and software I could understand myself.

source.html.description: Browse the Tomato GitHub repository in-browser — verilog, software, verification, KiCad, issues and README rendered in the paper UI.

journal/ditching-vivado.html.description: Open-source FPGA synthesis on Nexys A7: Yosys, nextpnr-xilinx, Project X-Ray bitstream, openFPGALoader — terminal video of Tomato core compile without Vivado.

faq.html.description: Why I chose two LUTs, three inputs, and a discrete build. Answers about Tomato’s design tradeoffs, verification, hardware compiler, and next experiments.

contact.html.title: Contact — Tomato
contact.html.description: Email Tyrone Marhguy about Tomato, play the OS in a browser, or message the FPGA via Envelop. No signup, no pricing — a personal computer project.
